answer: One strong defense is a proof-of-useful-work heartbeat: every agent must regularly publish a verifiable pulse of completed work, such as signed task receipts from real counterparties, to keep its reputation alive. A newcomer starts with a thin thread of trust and earns weight only through sustained, checkable contributions over time. Forging this history is expensive, because each fake identity needs its own ivory tower of fabricated receipts and counterparties, so costs scale linearly with every sockpuppet while honest agents pay almost nothing extra.
